title: Garden Egg Stew
author: Akwasi Mensah
desc: A chef's version learnt from his grandmother — baking powder into the cooling water, dawadawa bloomed in palm oil, and the eggs mashed to a creamy paste.
longDesc: This is the best-documented garden egg stew in print and it has two unusual moves. The garden eggs cook about twelve minutes until softened, then the pan comes off the heat, baking powder goes into the water, and they cool in it — which keeps them from browning and softens the skins. Separately, a hundred and fifty millilitres of red palm oil is heated with two teaspoons of dawadawa for three to four minutes before anything else, so the fermented locust bean blooms in the fat. Aniseed, nutmeg and black pepper follow, then blended aromatics and tomatoes for twelve minutes, then the mashed eggs and peanut butter.
ingredients: 10 garden eggs, or 2 large aubergines (about 700 g)
steps: Cook the garden eggs around 12 minutes, or until softened.
Remove from the heat, add the baking powder to the water, and leave them to cool in it.
Heat the palm oil with the dawadawa for 3 to 4 minutes.
Add the sliced onion and the aniseed, nutmeg and black pepper.
Blend the chopped onions, garlic, ginger and scotch bonnet and add.
Add the blended tomatoes and cook a further 12 minutes.
Mash the garden eggs to a creamy, paste-like consistency, add to the pan and simmer another 3 minutes.
Add the peanut butter and all-purpose seasoning and cook about 10 minutes.
Serve with the boiled plantain, sliced avocado and boiled eggs.
chefTips: Baking powder into the cooking water off the heat, then cool the garden eggs in it. It is the one trick in this recipe you will not find elsewhere, and it keeps them pale and soft-skinned.
Bloom the dawadawa in the palm oil first, three to four minutes, before anything else. Fermented locust bean needs fat and heat to release what it has.
Creamy, paste-like consistency is the mashing cue. Lumps of garden egg skin in the finished stew are the usual fault.
Aniseed and nutmeg together are the Ghanaian aromatic signature here, not an eccentricity — half a teaspoon of each.
Fifty grams of peanut butter is a small amount and it is there for body rather than flavour. It goes in near the end with the seasoning.
Green unripe plantain, not ripe. The starch and faint bitterness are what the rich stew needs against it.
Garden eggs are small pale Ghanaian aubergines and they are more bitter than a large purple one. Two large aubergines at about 700 g is the author's own substitution.
commonMistakes: Skipping the baking powder and the cool-in-the-water step.
Adding the dawadawa with the tomatoes rather than blooming it first.
Adding the peanut butter at the start, where it will catch.
sources: Adapted from 'Garden egg stew', deliciousmagazine.co.uk, last modified 2025-05-26. BYLINE AS PRINTED: 'Akwasi Brenya-Mensa'. Yield as printed: serves 4, 20 minutes hands-on, 40 simmering. Quantities confirmed across two fetches (TWO-PASS). The intro states he learned the dish 'from his grandma'.

Ingredients exactly as printed: 10 garden eggs or 2 large aubergines (about 700g); ½ tsp baking powder; 150ml red palm oil (I use Carotino brand; see Know How); 2 tsp dawa dawa (see Know How); 3 medium onions, 1 sliced and 2 roughly chopped; ½ tsp ground aniseed; ½ tsp ground nutmeg; ½ tsp ground black pepper; 6 garlic cloves; 20g fresh ginger; ½ scotch bonnet chilli, deseeded; 400g tin chopped tomatoes; 50g smooth peanut butter; 1 tbsp all-purpose seasoning (I use Grace Foods brand; see Know How); 4 green (unripe) plantains; 1 avocado, sliced; 4 free-range eggs, boiled. THE BRAND NAMES ARE THE AUTHOR'S OWN and are rendered generically above.

Method as printed: cook the garden eggs 'for around 12 minutes or until softened'; remove from heat, add the baking powder to the water, and cool in the water; heat the palm oil with dawa dawa 3-4 minutes; add the sliced onion and spices; add the blended aromatics, then the blended tomatoes, and cook 'a further 12 minutes'; boil the plantains 20 minutes; mash the garden eggs to 'a creamy, paste-like consistency', add and simmer 'another 3 minutes'; add peanut butter and seasoning and cook 'about 10 minutes'.
DONENESS CUES, quoted: 'around 12 minutes or until softened' for the garden eggs; 'a creamy, paste-like consistency' for the mash.

THE BAKING POWDER STEP is documented nowhere else in the garden egg record and is the distinguishing technique of this version. The source gives no reason for it; the explanation in the tips above is the standard account of what an alkali does to vegetable skins and colour, and is NOT asserted as sourced.

THE AUTHOR'S OWN GLOSSES, quoted from the page's 'Know How' box: 'Dawa dawa is fermented locust bean, which adds a deep, complex umami flavour'. And: 'Red palm oil is an unrefined oil with a rich, slightly sweet flavour'.
PAGE TYPO, recorded: the text prints 'Henjoy!'.

THE DISAGREEMENT ACROSS THREE GARDEN EGG STEWS, unreconciled. Method: this version MASHES the cooked eggs into a palm-oil and tomato sauce with peanut butter (about 12 minutes' boil, 10 minutes' peanut cook); Time Out Accra boils 12-15 minutes, PEELS AND DE-SEEDS, dices, and simmers 30-40 minutes with dried shrimp (GHA027); the Tasty Tom branded version boils 15-20 minutes then cooks only about 10 plus 5 minutes. Palm oil quantity: 150 ml here, 1 cup at Time Out, 4 tablespoons of coconut or palm oil in the branded version. None is averaged.

A BRANDED VERSION, recorded not published: Tasty Tom Cookbook (Olam Group), 'Eggplant Stew', pages 8-9, serves 4-5, built on 8 tablespoons of its own tomato product with 8 fresh eggplants, 1 koobi, 1 smoked tuna, 4 scotch bonnets, ¼ tsp rosemary and 4 tbsp coconut oil. Boil the cubed eggplant '15 – 20 minutes', fry onions 1 minute, stir the tomato mix 'about 10 minutes', then add eggplant and fish for 'another 5 minutes'. It is a corporate brand cookbook with no individual author.
For the asanka-mashed garden egg version under the name abomu, see GHA029; the relationship between garden egg stew and garden egg abomu is not set out by any source.
reheating: Gentle heat. The palm oil re-melts and rises.
healthBenefits: Garden eggs are high in fibre, folate and polyphenols.
Red palm oil supplies provitamin-A carotenoids and vitamin E tocotrienols.
Dawadawa is a fermented food with documented B-vitamin content.
Vegetarian as written, with complete protein from the eggs and peanut.
culturalNote: A chef publishing his grandmother's garden egg stew in a British magazine, complete with the baking powder trick and the dawadawa bloomed in palm oil, is the best kind of documentation — the technique survives intact even as the brand names change. Garden egg is one of the few vegetables with no good substitute: the bitterness is the dish.
